The executive picture

Where to focus

Falls are a known risk in assisted living, and most of the region’s are steady. The one place that is moving is the Cedar Point evening shift (3 to 11 pm). In September it was understaffed on 19 of 30 evenings, up from 4 of 31 in July. Fourteen of the 17 evening falls at Cedar Point happened on those 19 evenings. The schedule is not the cause: the gaps open when a caregiver calls out and the open shift is posted late. Every Friday, Saturday and Sunday evening in September was understaffed.

Care story · July to September

What needs attention

Three layers: when the falls happen, where the gap is, and why it stays open.

Falls follow short staffing, not the calendar.

Cedar Point evenings · falls per evening, September
Fully staffed (11 evenings)
0.27 · 3 falls
Understaffed (19 evenings)
0.74 · 14 falls
Both bars use the same scale. Falls are evening-shift events in the Cedar Point record.

Cedar Point recorded 17 evening-shift falls in September. Fourteen of them were on the 19 evenings that were understaffed, and 3 were on the 11 evenings that were fully staffed. That is 0.74 falls per understaffed evening against 0.27 per fully staffed evening, almost three times the rate. Falls on the other shifts and in the other communities were steady.

Why it matters: This is a pattern in the records, not a finding about any one caregiver or resident. It shows where an ordinary risk grows. Owner: Cedar Point executive director.

The gap is one place, one shift, and it is growing.

The gap is not region-wide. Cedar Point was understaffed on 19 evenings; the other four communities together were understaffed on 6. At Cedar Point the gap has grown from 4 evenings in July to 9 in August and 19 in September. It follows the week: every Friday, Saturday and Sunday evening in September was understaffed (12 of 12), against 7 of 18 Monday to Thursday evenings.

Do: Treat Cedar Point’s Friday to Sunday evenings as the first place to add cover. Owner: Cedar Point executive director.

Late posting of open shifts is why the gaps stay open.

Cedar Point · open evening shifts left unfilled, September
Posted before noon (11 shifts)
1 unfilled · 9%
Posted after 1 pm (23 shifts)
18 unfilled · 78%
September’s 19 understaffed evenings · how the gap opened
18
Open shift posted after 1 pm: 18   ·   Posted before noon: 1

The schedule itself is complete. The gaps open when a caregiver calls out and the open shift is posted late. Of the 19 understaffed evenings, 18 began with an open shift posted after 1 pm. Those shifts went unfilled 78 percent of the time. Shifts posted before noon went unfilled 9 percent of the time. Open shifts posted after 1 pm go to the manager on duty, and on Friday to Sunday that manager is the only person who can post them.

Do: Add a standby caregiver for Cedar Point’s Friday to Sunday evenings, about 12 standby shifts a month. Send any call-out after 1 pm to the float pool within 30 minutes. Owner: Cedar Point executive director and regional operations.
